newsitem.title: USA: Hedge funds turn cautious in May, underperform mkt.
newsitem.headline: Hedge funds turn cautious in May, underperform mkt.

text.p: Hedge funds, said to be inherently risky, took a decidely cautious approach in May, leading them to underperform most leading investment indices during the month, a hedge fund investment advisory firm reported on Thursday.
According to Nashville-based Van Hedge Fund Advisors Inc, the average U.S. hedge fund gained 4.7 percent, while the average offshore hedge fund gained 3.1 percent in May.
He said hedge fund managers agreed that the market is overvalued, "floating on a balloon of excessive optimism."

"For many of these managers, the only question is when the balloon will pop, with some saying that a significant correction may occur as soon as July, when the (Federal Reserve) meets to decide whether or not interest rates will be increased," Van said.

U.S. value hedge funds, which returned 7.2 percent on average during May, outperformed all other hedge fund investment styles worldwide during the month. U.S. aggressive growth funds were second with an average return of 7.0 percent.
That compares with a 6.1 percent increase in the S&P 500, a 7.5 percent gain by the average U.S. equity mutual fund and a 1.0 percent increase in the average U.S. bond mutual fund, said the firm.

"Notwithstanding the excellent performance achieved by a few hedge fund investment strategies during May, hedge funds as a group apparently have decided that the equity markets are simply too unstable to warrant risking their investors' capital for the sake of a few additional points in monthly performance," said George Van, the firm's president, in a statment.
